recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future question about whether the remaining secondary SNOMED CT Temperature taking coding is pedagogically useful should be handled by a new OO tracker rather than FHIR-7231.
issue_request: FHIR-7231 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO issue for the DSTU1 Observation f202 temperature example. It objected that SNOMED CT oral-temperature and LOINC body-temperature codings were shown together without alignment/explanation, and resolved to edit examples so SNOMED-only Observation.code content was handled by adding LOINC translations or making the code local.
initial_application: Git commit 474be19befc8b8882da2b23a826dd0e2106a1538 explicitly listed 7231 and changed the f202 example by replacing SNOMED CT 415945006 in Observation.code with a local acme.lab BT coding, keeping LOINC 8310-5, and changing the body site to Oral cavity. Later edits added explanatory international-coding text and restored the LOINC 8310-5 coding to Observation.code after Vital Signs refactoring.
additional_context: FHIR-7211 is the same f202 temperature issue family and is explicitly referenced by FHIR-7231 as core #271. FHIR-7211 clarifies that FHIR core is international and not limited to LOINC, so the accepted decision does not require removing every SNOMED CT coding. source/fhir.ini lists Observation as an active resource, and current f202 includes LOINC 8310-5, local BT, and LOINC 8331-1 while omitting the original SNOMED CT 415945006 coding. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative source already removes the original mismatched SNOMED oral-temperature Observation.code coding and includes the LOINC/local coding alignment requested by the issue.
